context.analysis:
## Overview
[The system modernizes a regional insurer's claims platform by gradually replacing a 30-year-old mainframe system with a cloud-native solution while maintaining hybrid operations. Its core purpose is to enable online claim submission and adjuster workflows while ensuring data consistency and continuous legacy fallback.]

## Key Elements
• New Insurance Platform (Azure Kubernetes Service, .NET/Java microservices)
• Legacy Mainframe (COBOL/DB2, On-Premises System of Record)
• Integration Gateway / Anti-Corruption Layer (Asynchronous Messaging)
• External Actors (Customers, Brokers, Claims Adjusters)
• External Systems (Azure Active Directory, Payment Gateway, Notification Service)

## Relationships
• Customers & Brokers interact with New Insurance Platform via HTTPS / Web UI for online submissions
• Claims Adjusters interact with New Insurance Platform via HTTPS for internal workflows
• New Insurance Platform integrates with Legacy Mainframe via Asynchronous Messaging through Integration Gateway
• New Insurance Platform authenticates users via OpenID Connect / OAuth 2.1 with Azure Active Directory
• New Insurance Platform communicates with Payment Gateway and Notification Service via REST/HTTPS APIs with mTLS

## Technology Stack
• Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS): Manages microservices workloads for cloud scalability
• Azure Active Directory: Enforces single sign-on (SSO) and hybrid identity management
• Azure Key Vault: Secures and rotates credentials, eliminating hardcoded secrets
• Azure ExpressRoute & IPsec VPN: Secures hybrid network connectivity between Azure and on-prem data center
• Asynchronous Messaging (Kafka / Azure Service Bus): Decouples services to respect the nightly batch window and protect legacy schemas

## Rationale
[This hybrid architecture satisfies the strict three-year migration constraint and protects expensive mainframe interfaces using an asynchronous integration gateway. It mitigates the team's low cloud experience by leveraging managed Azure services while ensuring zero data loss and rapid one-day fallback capabilities.]

containers.analysis:
## Overview
[The system modernizes a 30-year-old regional insurer mainframe claims platform by gradually migrating claim types to a hybrid cloud architecture. It enables online submissions and fast adjuster workflows while maintaining the legacy COBOL/DB2 system as the system of record.]

## Key Elements
- Customers & Brokers
- Claims Adjusters
- Customer Portal (SPA React)
- Adjuster Workspace (SPA React)
- API Gateway (Azure API Management)
- Claims Core Container (.NET / Azure Container Apps)
- Read Model Projector (Azure Functions / .NET)
- Integration & ACL Container (Azure Functions)
- Adjuster Read Database (Azure Cosmos DB)
- Legacy Mainframe (COBOL/DB2 / CICS)
- Message Broker (IBM MQ)
- Identity Provider (Azure Active Directory)

## Relationships
- Customers & Brokers interact with Customer Portal via HTTPS/REST
- Claims Adjusters interact with Adjuster Workspace via HTTPS/REST
- Customer Portal & Adjuster Workspace authenticate via Azure Active Directory using OpenID Connect/OAuth 2.0
- API Gateway routes frontend traffic to Claims Core Container via HTTPS
- Claims Core Container reads/writes data and publishes events
- Read Model Projector updates Adjuster Read Database via internal messaging
- Integration & ACL Container communicates with Legacy Mainframe via IBM MQ with mTLS

## Technology Stack
- Azure App Service / Azure Container Apps: Runs frontend SPAs and backend .NET core services to offset team's low cloud experience
- Azure API Management: Secures and routes external traffic with OAuth 2.0 and RBAC
- Azure Cosmos DB / PostgreSQL: Provides low-latency CQRS read storage for sub-2s UI loads
- Azure Functions (.NET): Executes asynchronous event projections and ACL data translation
- IBM MQ: Manages asynchronous message exchange across the hybrid cloud-to-mainframe perimeter
- OpenTelemetry: Ensures centralized distributed tracing across hybrid Azure and on-premise boundaries

## Rationale
[This hybrid architecture isolates expensive mainframe changes behind an Anti-Corruption Layer while delivering sub-2-second adjuster response times via a CQRS pattern. It leverages managed Azure PaaS services to safely scale capabilities for a team with limited cloud experience.]

Customer Portal.analysis:
## Overview
[The Customer Portal provides a modern React-based web interface for customers and brokers to submit insurance claims online. It integrates with Azure services and legacy systems via an API gateway.]

## Key Elements
- [Customer Portal (React SPA)]
- [Authentication Controller (TypeScript / MSAL.js)]
- [Claim Submission Wizard (React Component / Formik)]
- [Document Uploader Component (React)]
- [API Client Service (Axios / Fetch)]
- [Azure Static Web Apps / CDN]
- [Azure Active Directory]
- [Azure Blob Storage]

## Relationships
- [Customers & Brokers -> Customer Portal: Interacts for online submissions [HTTPS/REST]]
- [Authentication Controller -> Azure Active Directory: Authenticates users and acquires tokens [OpenID Connect / OAuth 2.0]]
- [Claim Submission Wizard -> API Client Service: Submits claim payloads [HTTPS/REST]]
- [Claim Submission Wizard -> Document Uploader Component: Initiates file attachments [HTTPS]]
- [Document Uploader Component -> Azure Blob Storage: Uploads binaries directly [HTTPS/PUT via Pre-signed URLs]]
- [Customer Portal -> Azure Static Web Apps / CDN: Serves static frontend assets [HTTPS]]

## Technology Stack
- [React & TypeScript: Frontend UI components and type safety]
- [MSAL.js: In-memory token management with Auth Code Flow + PKCE]
- [Azure Static Web Apps & CDN: Stateless static hosting and global delivery]
- [Azure Blob Storage: Secure binary file attachments using pre-signed URLs]
- [Terraform / Bicep: Infrastructure as Code for environment provisioning and CORS rules]

## Rationale
[This architecture secures client-side interactions and protects backend gateways by offloading large file uploads directly to storage. It accommodates low cloud experience through standardized static hosting and managed infrastructure templates.]

Adjuster Workspace.analysis:
## Overview
[The Insurance Claims Modernization system gradually replaces a 30-year-old mainframe with a modern hybrid cloud platform. It ensures seamless parallel processing of claims while maintaining strict performance, security, and data consistency.]

## Key Elements
- Claims Adjusters & Customers/Brokers
- Adjuster Workspace (SPA React)
- API Gateway (Azure API Management)
- Claims Core Container (.NET / Azure Container Apps)
- Azure Active Directory & Azure Cosmos DB

## Relationships
- Claims Adjusters -> Adjuster Workspace: Interacts for internal workflows [HTTPS/REST]
- Adjuster Workspace -> Azure Active Directory: Authenticates users [OpenID Connect / OAuth 2.0 with PKCE]
- Adjuster Workspace -> API Gateway: Routes state-changing intents [HTTPS/TLS 1.3]
- Optimized Read Store Client -> Azure Cosmos DB: Queries cached projections directly using ephemeral resource tokens [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- React SPA: Chosen for responsive UI development within the Adjuster Workspace.
- Azure Cosmos DB: Provides low-latency storage for read projections to meet <2s load times.
- Azure API Management: Secures and routes backend communications.
- Azure Active Directory: Enables enterprise SSO integration (R-07).

## Rationale
[This architecture decouples the legacy mainframe from the modern UI, enabling high-performance adjuster workflows through dedicated read models while preserving system consistency. The hybrid approach allows incremental claim-type migration with minimal risk.]

API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
The system is a hybrid cloud platform that modernizes a 30-year-old regional insurer mainframe claims system. It incrementally migrates claim types while keeping the legacy system as the system of record.

## Key Elements
- Customer Portal (React SPA)
- Adjuster Workspace (React SPA)
- API Gateway (Azure API Management) with Authentication Validator, Dynamic Route Orchestrator, Rate Limiter & Circuit Breaker, and Claim-Type Feature Flag Evaluator
- Claims Core Container (.NET / Azure Container Apps)
- Integration & ACL Container (Azure Functions)
- Read Model Projector (Azure Functions / .NET)
- Adjuster Read Database (Azure Cosmos DB)
- Message Broker (IBM MQ)
- Azure Active Directory

## Relationships
- Customer Portal -> API Gateway: Routes frontend traffic [HTTPS]
- Adjuster Workspace -> API Gateway: Routes frontend traffic [HTTPS]
- API Gateway -> Azure Active Directory: Validates JWT tokens [OpenID Connect]
- API Gateway -> Claims Core Container: Forwards requests and enforces mTLS [HTTPS / Mutual TLS]
- API Gateway -> Integration & ACL Container: Forwards unmigrated and fallback claim requests [HTTPS / JSON]

## Technology Stack
- Azure API Management: Edge routing, rate limiting, and mTLS enforcement to secure downstream services.
- Azure Container Apps (.NET): Hosts scalable modern claims core processing logic.
- Azure Functions: Executes asynchronous read projections and integration/ACL translation.
- Azure Cosmos DB: Provides low-latency read models for adjuster screens.
- Azure Active Directory: Delivers centralized Single Sign-On and identity management.
- IBM MQ: Handles asynchronous message brokering with the legacy mainframe.

## Rationale
The hybrid architecture protects the fragile legacy mainframe using an API Gateway circuit breaker and rate limiter while enabling incremental claim type migration. It satisfies strict performance and security constraints by isolating modernization changes and leveraging managed Azure cloud services.

Claims Core Container.analysis:
## Overview
[The Claims Core Container processes modernized and legacy claims using .NET on Azure Container Apps. It gradually replaces an on-premise mainframe while maintaining consistency and compliance.]

## Key Elements
- Claim Intake Controller (`ASP.NET Core API`)
- Claim Workflow Engine (`MassTransit / .NET`)
- Legacy Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL) Adapter (`IBM MQ`)
- Claim Domain Service (`C# / Domain-Driven Design`)
- Data Storage (`Azure SQL Database`)

## Relationships
- Claim Intake Controller -> Claim Workflow Engine: Dispatches commands (`In-Memory / MediatR`)
- Claim Workflow Engine -> Legacy ACL Adapter: Delegates unmigrated types (`AMQP / IBM MQ`)
- Claim Workflow Engine -> Message Broker: Emits domain events (`AMQP`)
- Claim Domain Service -> Azure SQL Database: Reads/Writes domain state (`Entity Framework Core / TDS`)

## Technology Stack
- .NET on Azure Container Apps: Chosen for core application runtime.
- MassTransit: Implements event-driven messaging and workflow routing.
- Azure SQL Database: Provides persistent transactional storage with Outbox pattern support.
- IBM MQ: Enables hybrid connectivity to the legacy on-premise mainframe.

## Rationale
[This architecture uses a modular internal design and Anti-Corruption Layer to safely isolate legacy mainframe dependencies. It enables gradual claim type migration while meeting strict consistency, rollback, and security requirements.]
Claims Core Container.yaml_definition:
level: component
scope: "Component diagram for the Claims Core Container container"
parentContainer:

Read Model Projector.analysis:
## Overview
[The system modernizes a 30-year-old mainframe claims system through a hybrid cloud architecture while legacy processing continues. The Read Model Projector component asynchronously updates read models to ensure low-latency adjuster screens.]

## Key Elements
- Event Consumer Component (Azure Functions / .NET) with Checkpoint & Idempotency Filter
- Projection Handler Component (.NET Class Library)
- Database Writer Component (.NET / Cosmos DB SDK)
- Message Broker (IBM MQ)
- Adjuster Read Database (Azure Cosmos DB)

## Relationships
- Message Broker -> Event Consumer: Pulls domain events [AMQP / IBM MQ]
- Event Consumer -> Projection Handler: Dispatches raw payloads [In-memory C# calls]
- Projection Handler -> Database Writer: Sends transformed read models [In-memory C# calls]
- Database Writer -> Adjuster Read Database: Persists state and secures private connectivity [HTTPS / Cosmos DB SDK over Private Endpoints]

## Technology Stack
- Azure Functions (.NET): Chosen for serverless execution to mitigate the team's limited cloud experience.
- Azure Cosmos DB: Provides partitioned storage to achieve adjuster screen loads under 2 seconds.
- IBM MQ: Handles reliable enterprise messaging and event distribution.
- OpenTelemetry & Application Insights: Tracks distributed tracing, consumer lag, and projection latency.
- Azure Managed Identity & VNet Integration: Enforces zero-trust security and secretless authentication.

## Rationale
[This decoupled, serverless architecture simplifies cloud adoption while satisfying stringent performance and consistency requirements. Robust idempotency filters and private networking ensure zero data loss and regulatory compliance during incremental migration.]

Integration & ACL Container.analysis:
## Overview
The hybrid system modernizes a 30-year-old regional insurer mainframe by gradually migrating claim types to a cloud-native platform. It maintains uninterrupted legacy operations while ensuring zero data loss and robust multi-system consistency.

## Key Elements
- Customers & Brokers
- Claims Adjusters
- Customer Portal & Adjuster Workspace (SPA React)
- API Gateway (Azure API Management)
- Claims Core Container (.NET / Azure Container Apps)
- Integration & ACL Container (Azure Container Apps)
- Read Model Projector (Azure Functions / .NET)
- Adjuster Read Database (Azure Cosmos DB)
- Message Broker (IBM MQ)
- Legacy Mainframe (COBOL/DB2)
- Azure Active Directory & Azure Key Vault

## Relationships
- Customer Portal & Adjuster Workspace -> API Gateway: HTTPS/REST
- API Gateway -> Claims Core Container: HTTPS/gRPC
- Claims Core Container -> Message Broker (IBM MQ): AMQP
- Integration & ACL Container -> Message Broker (IBM MQ): AMQP
- Mainframe Adapter -> Legacy Mainframe: IBM MQ with mTLS over Azure ExpressRoute/VPN
- Integration & Adjuster Workspace -> Azure Active Directory: OpenID Connect / OAuth 2.0

## Technology Stack
- Azure Container Apps: Standardizes runtime and reduces cognitive load for low-cloud-experience teams.
- .NET / C#: Powers core services and internal ACL components for domain modeling.
- IBM MQ: Ensures reliable asynchronous messaging during migrations and legacy batch windows.
- Azure Cosmos DB: Provides low-latency storage for the adjuster read model (<2s UI load requirement).
- Azure Key Vault & Managed Identities: Secures mTLS certificates and eliminates hardcoded credentials.

## Rationale
This hybrid architecture isolates expensive legacy mainframe touchpoints behind an Anti-Corruption Layer while modernizing the user-facing experience. It guarantees zero data loss and enables 1-day rollbacks per claim type using proven enterprise patterns and unified container runtimes.

Adjuster Read Database.analysis:
## Overview
The Adjuster Read Database provides a high-performance CQRS read model using Azure Cosmos DB to enable sub-2-second UI load times for claims adjusters. It supports a hybrid cloud migration strategy while ensuring zero data loss and strict security compliance.

## Key Elements
- Cosmos DB SQL API Container: Azure Cosmos DB instance hosting the read model
- Claims Collection: Cosmos DB Container partitioned by `ClaimId` for optimized query distribution
- Audit Collection: Cosmos DB Container storing immutable change logs for tracing
- Change Feed Processor: Cosmos DB Change Feed for downstream auditing and triggers
- Private Endpoint: Azure Private Endpoint ensuring isolated network access

## Relationships
- Read Model Projector -> Claims Collection: Upserts denormalized documents via [Cosmos DB SDK / TCP]
- API Gateway -> Claims Collection: Executes point-reads and queries via [Cosmos DB SDK / TCP]
- Read Model Projector -> Change Feed Processor: Triggers event processing via [Cosmos DB Change Feed]

## Technology Stack
- Azure Cosmos DB (SQL API): Selected for global distribution and low-latency NoSQL document storage meeting R-05 performance requirements
- Azure AD RBAC & Managed Identities: Replaces master key connection strings for secure least-privilege access
- Azure Key Vault: Provides Customer-Managed Keys (CMK) for encryption at rest for data and backups
- Azure Virtual Network & Private Endpoints: Secures database traffic by disabling public network access

## Rationale
This architecture resolves the team's lack of cloud experience by enforcing strict infrastructure-as-code, continuous backups, and private networking. It guarantees high availability, sub-2s query performance, and robust security isolation required during the legacy mainframe migration.

Message Broker.analysis:
## Overview
Modernizes a regional insurer's legacy mainframe claims system via a hybrid cloud platform while preserving core operations. It gradually migrates claim types over three years without extending nightly batch windows.

## Key Elements
- Users: Customers, Brokers, Claims Adjusters
- Frontend: Customer Portal (React SPA), Adjuster Workspace (React SPA)
- Gateway & Routing: Azure API Management, Outbound Topic Router
- Core Services: Claims Core Container (.NET), Read Model Projector (Azure Functions), Integration & ACL Container
- Messaging & Storage: IBM MQ (Message Broker), Azure Cosmos DB (Adjuster Read Database)
- Security & Infrastructure: Azure Active Directory, Azure Key Vault, Azure Monitor / Sentinel

## Relationships
- Customer Portal / Adjuster Workspace -> Azure API Management: Handles HTTPS/REST traffic [REST/TLS]
- Claims Core Container -> Outbound Topic Router: Publishes domain events [IBM MQ / AMQP]
- Outbound Topic Router -> Integration & ACL Container: Forwards legacy sync events [IBM MQ]
- Message Broker -> Azure Monitor / Sentinel: Streams security audit logs [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- Cloud Platform: Azure West Europe & On-Premise Hybrid (for low cloud-experience team transition)
- Backend Compute: Azure Container Apps, Azure Functions (.NET)
- Messaging: IBM MQ (enables hybrid on-premise mainframe to Azure bridging)
- Database: Azure Cosmos DB (supports <2s adjuster screen loads)
- Security: OAuth 2.0 / JWT, Mutual TLS (mTLS), Azure Key Vault (for zero-loss and strict access control)

## Rationale
This hybrid architecture isolates expensive mainframe dependencies while enabling gradual claim migration within strict consistency constraints. Standardized Azure and IBM MQ technologies mitigate the team's low cloud experience risks.
